data.description:
## Goal

Reduce the fast-mode idle dispatch lease from 30s to 15s so the single fast slot is released sooner after a session's last request, cutting `local_lease_active` fallbacks (79 in window) and inter-turn dispatch denials (163 total), raising local capture and busy time.

## Context (from parent LP-0MV8805WF007LTZA)

- Base `server.local_dispatch_lease_timeout_seconds: 30` (config.yaml). 30s = a fixed post-stream cooldown; an idle session holds the slot until the timeout.
- History: 15s was tested earlier but raised back to 30s as a safety net after a 15x increase in mid-request orphan cleanups (LP-0MSKOHV55003XFTB). The root causes were subsequently addressed by the prefill-progress liveness extension, anonymous chunk-refresh buffer, and active-slot orphan verification (LP-0MSUO5Z0K007HBSS, LP-0MSUO6HLX0089MNQ, LP-0MSUO6XRP001MCB2) — so 15s is worth re-testing **fast-only** (fast runs 1 slot; cheap keeps 30s).
- Log analysis of an earlier window (LP-0MSKLI4FH0082TEB) showed 100% of dispatch denies were caused by idle lease holders, never GPU saturation; inter-turn reclaim gaps were median 0.2s / p90 0.7s — far below 30s.

## Change

`proxy/config-fast.yaml` (overlay deep-merges over base):

```yaml
server:
  local_dispatch_lease_timeout_seconds: 15
```

Cheap and base stay at 30.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `proxy/config-fast.yaml` adds `server.local_dispatch_lease_timeout_seconds: 15` in the worktree, with the fast-mode golden fixtures updated in lockstep (`proxy/tests/fixtures/merged_config_fast.json` and `prededup_raw_fast.json` move 30→15) and `TestDeduplicatedModeFiles.test_residue_server_keys` fast key-set extended, so the config-merge golden suite still passes (build → test → commit order).
- [ ] Verify in the fast-mode proxy log that leases expire at ~15s and `local_lease_active` / `local_dispatch_denied` events drop vs baseline (79 / 163).
- [ ] No regression in orphan cleanups: mid-request `dispatch_first_byte_timeout` / orphan-cleanup events must not spike vs the 15s-test baseline (LP-0MSKOHV55003XFTB documented the failure signature — check for it explicitly).
- [ ] Local busy time / capture rate rise over the post-change window (proxy-usage-analysis report).
- [ ] Keep/revert decision recorded with evidence.

## Risks

- Mid-request lease expiry on long silent generations (released early → orphan cleanup → client retry → full re-prefill). Mitigated by chunk-refresh (30s buffer) and prefill liveness extension, but fast's single slot makes a wrong timeout costly — this is why the change is fast-only and evaluated separately from Stage 1.

**Key Files:**
- `proxy/config-fast.yaml`
- `proxy/config.yaml` (base — unchanged at 30)
- `proxy/tests/fixtures/merged_config_fast.json`
- `proxy/tests/fixtures/prededup_raw_fast.json`
- `proxy/tests/test_config_merge.py`
data.title: Fast-mode idle dispatch lease 30s->15s (config-fast.yaml)

data.description:
## Goal

Determine how often the llama-proxy flips between **fast** and **cheap** modes,
what triggers each flip (in particular the ContextHub/herdr code that initiates
the switch to fast), whether the flip rate is problematic, and what (if
anything) should change to reduce it.

## Context / findings so far

Investigation of the 24h window 2026-10-14 14:02 → 2026-10-15 14:02 UTC found
**30 proxy restarts**, of which **15 were "Mode-switch restart spawned"**
(one restart per real mode transition).

Trigger sources identified:

- **ContextHub / herdr** — `../ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts`:
  - *Fast on command*: records operator activity and fire-and-forget
    `POST /admin/set-mode {"mode":"fast"}`.
  - *Cheap on idle*: leader-only, when idle ≥
    `DEFAULT_MODE_SWITCH_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS` (900_000 ms = 15 min) **and** the
    proxy reports idle, gated by the model-cooldown signal.
  - Shared activity broadcast via `mode-activity.json`; leader elected via the
    downtime worker; fail-closed everywhere.
- **Proxy's built-in time schedule** — `proxy/mode_schedule.yaml`
  (cheap 01:00, fast 10:00) = 2/day.
- **Manual** `POST /admin/set-mode` (operators/agents).

Each real transition persists the mode and spawns
`proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh --restart` (`proxy/proxy/mode.py` `set_mode()` →
`_spawn_restart()`), because fast/cheap are separate config profiles
(`config-fast.yaml` vs `config-cheap.yaml`) with different slot-pool sizes
(fast: base `session_slot_pool_size: 1`; cheap: 3). The restart re-inits
llama-server and typically yields a ~60s local-qwen3 cooldown on a cold-start
503. Redundant switches are skipped (mode already matches), so transition count
== restart-contribution count.

**Is this period unusual?** Historical per-calendar-day mode-switch counts from
the rotated logs: 10-08=28, 10-09=22, 10-10=16, 10-11=10, 10-12=32, 10-13=24,
10-14=31, 10-15=19 (partial, ~14h). So flipping is **endemic (~10–34/day)** —
to be confirmed and extended in this investigation.

## Questions to answer

1. How many flips/day, split by trigger source (ContextHub fast-on-command,
   ContextHub idle-cheap, proxy schedule, manual)?
2. Is the fast-on-command path firing repeatedly during active periods
   (flip-flop)? Quantify fast→cheap→fast pairs within short windows.
3. What is the cost per flip (restart duration, local cooldown, dropped or
   retried in-flight work, cold-prefill thunder)?
4. What else (besides mode) causes the proxy to restart, and how much of the
   flip rate is attributable to each?
5. What options exist to reduce flipping (e.g. minimum-dwell/hysteresis, keep
   fast during working hours rather than idle-cheap, only switch when the
   benefit is real, coalesce/defer switches, non-destructive switch), with
   trade-offs?
6. Recommendation: act or not, and if so, what and with what measurable target?

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Flip frequency over ≥7 days of logs is documented (per-day counts +
      intra-day distribution), separated by trigger source.
- [ ] The ContextHub `mode-switch-worker.ts` switching logic is documented
      (triggers, gates, thresholds, leader election, cooldown gate, fail-closed
      behaviour).
- [ ] A quantified answer to "was the studied 24h period unusual?" against the
      ≥7-day baseline.
- [ ] A cost-per-flip estimate (restart duration, local cooldown, in-flight
      impact, cold-prefill effect).
- [ ] A prioritised list of reduction options with expected effect and
      trade-offs, and at least one recommended option with a measurable target.
- [ ] Follow-up implementation work items are created for the recommended
      option(s), or a decision not to act is recorded.
- [ ] Evidence is command/log based and reproducible (exact greps/scripts
      recorded in this item).

## References

- Related items: LP-0MSM5K4TX004MICX (time-based schedule),
  LP-0MSMF5LXO006YDNM (in-flight sessions across mode switches),
  LP-0MSMFQ3DL006EY2H (grandfathered routing tests).
- Code: `proxy/proxy/mode.py`, `proxy/mode_schedule.yaml`,
  `../ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts`.
- Logs: `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*`.
data.title: Investigate fast<->cheap proxy mode-flip frequency and how to reduce it (ContextHub trigger focus)

data.description:
## Goal

Determine empirically whether **fast** and **cheap** modes can share a single
`session_slot_pool_size` (test 3, 2, 1 slots) so a mode switch no longer
requires a destructive full proxy + llama-server restart; if a single slot
count is not viable, design and implement a drain-based mode switch.

## Context / findings so far

- fast (base `proxy/config.yaml`): `session_slot_pool_size: 1`; cheap
  (`proxy/config-cheap.yaml`): `session_slot_pool_size: 3`.
- The restart on switch exists because slot count (and model profile) differ
  between the two profiles.
- Contention evidence: in the fast-mode (1-slot) window 10:00–14:02 UTC there
  were 173 `fallback_after_queue` local fallbacks; cheap-mode (3-slot)
  01:00–10:00 had 207 over a longer window. 39 `empty_response` cooldowns in
  24h cluster under 1-slot contention.
- Large contexts already bypass local (`large_context_bypass` /
  `context_too_large`, 400–750/day), so the local slot mostly serves small
  requests — relevant when judging smaller per-slot context at higher N.

## Approach

1. Benchmark local Qwen3 at 1, 2 and 3 slots under representative
   concurrent-session load (≥ the observed concurrency of 2–3 active sessions
   plus queue depth), measuring throughput, latency/TTFT, queue-timeout rate,
   local stream share, and local quarantine episodes.
2. Decide whether one slot count is viable for both modes.
3. If viable: create a work item to converge the configs and make the mode
   switch non-destructive (keep llama-server + warm KV cache, reusing the
   existing llama-server adopt/reuse machinery in `lifecycle.py`
   LP-0MUCEFCL6001ZXYN).
4. If not viable: design + implement a drain-based switch (defer new requests,
   let in-flight local streams finish up to a bounded deadline
   `mode_switch_drain.max_seconds`, then switch), with tests.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Benchmark results for 1/2/3 slots are recorded (reproducible commands,
      configs, raw numbers) with throughput/latency/queue-timeout/local-share.
- [ ] A recommendation states whether a single slot count is viable for both
      modes, the chosen N, and the measured trade-offs (per-slot context,
      memory, decode speed, contention).
- [ ] If viable: a follow-up work item is created to converge slot counts and
      remove the restart-on-switch.
- [ ] If not viable: a drain-based switch is specified and, once authorised,
      implemented with tests covering: new-request deferral, bounded in-flight
      drain, timeout behaviour, and no client-visible `finish_reason: error`.
- [ ] The evaluation accounts for the large-context bypass traffic
      (400–750/day) in interpreting per-slot context trade-offs.
- [ ] Full suite passes via /skill:test before any implementation is committed.

## References

- Related items: LP-0MRWJIBIE0012HDD (slot-count benchmark: optimal pool size),
  LP-0MRW0WTOO002GG8I (pool 2 → 6), LP-0MQMH0WHY005UPFA (align pool with
  llama-server --parallel), LP-0MRDE669Y003V1SO (cache-cold after restart),
  LP-0MSM3TGO3007QN9M (mode control UI).
- Code: `proxy/config.yaml`, `proxy/config-cheap.yaml`, `proxy/config-fast.yaml`,
  `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` (llama-server reuse / adopt),
  `proxy/proxy/mode.py` (`_spawn_restart`, drain).
data.title: Evaluate performance impact of equalising fast/cheap slot counts (3/2/1); if not viable implement a drain

data.description:
## Goal

Implement **grace-period immunity** so a local (Qwen3) HTTP 503 or connection
failure during the post-restart warm-up / cold-start window does **not** apply
the standard `provider_cooldown_seconds: 60` quarantine to `local-qwen3`.
During warm-up the failure is "not ready yet", not a provider fault: the
request should be deferred (Retry-After) and local should become eligible as
soon as it is ready.

## Context / mechanism (verified)

- After a proxy restart, requests that race llama-server warm-up are denied
  (`local_dispatch_denied ... cold_start=True`) and the backend returns
  **HTTP 503** → `Fallback triggered ... reason=HTTP 503` →
  `provider_cooldown_seconds: 60` quarantine on local, e.g.
  2026-10-15 13:19:56 → 13:20:56 cooldown.
- This is the dominant cause of the ~60s local quarantines seen repeatedly
  (12 of 45 episodes in the studied 24h window followed a restart within 75s).
- Existing knobs to reuse: `local_cold_start_retry_after_seconds` (default 15),
  `local_cold_start_max_concurrent` (default 1), the router grace-window
  readiness signal ("Router model ... became available during grace window").
- Related completed work: LP-0MR01SJBP005I0OR (fallback not recovering after
  model-loading 503).

## Design constraints

- Local failures while cold-starting / not ready must NOT call
  `mark_provider_unavailable()` with the standard cooldown, and must NOT feed
  the exponential-backoff failure counter; they should defer using
  `local_cold_start_retry_after_seconds`.
- The readiness/warm-up signal must be explicit and bounded (no magic sleeps):
  e.g. a warm-up window anchored to service start or a readiness probe, which
  ends when the model is confirmed ready.
- A genuine, sustained 503 **after** warm-up must still quarantine local as
  today (do not mask real failures).
- Behaviour applies per restart event (a new warm-up window begins on each
  restart), and must interact correctly with concurrent cold-start dispatch
  gating (`local_cold_start_max_concurrent`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A deterministic test reproduces the current cold-start 503 → 60s
      cooldown, then verifies it no longer occurs after the change.
- [ ] Tests cover: (a) cold-start 503 within the warm-up window → defer, no
      cooldown; (b) sustained 503 after warm-up → normal cooldown; (c)
      connection error during warm-up → defer, no cooldown; (d) concurrent
      cold-start dispatch gating still respected; (e) a fresh warm-up window
      begins after each restart.
- [ ] Failure-counter / exponential-backoff state is not polluted during the
      warm-up window.
- [ ] No regression in routing/fallback tests; full suite passes via
      /skill:test before commit.
- [ ] Follows the implement workflow (worktree, build → test → commit).
- [ ] Logs/metrics evidence pre/post: local cooldown episodes in the hour after
      a restart drop to ~0 (see evaluation in the sibling investigation items).

## References

- Related items: LP-0MR01SJBP005I0OR, and the sibling items for mode-flip
  frequency and restart examination (to validate pre/post impact).
- Code: `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (`_handle_http_error_with_cooldown`,
  `_handle_connection_error_in_fallback`, `mark_provider_unavailable`,
  cold-start admission / `local_cold_start_*`), `proxy/config.yaml`
  (`local_cold_start_*`, `provider_cooldown_seconds`).
data.title: Implement grace-period immunity: local cold-start 503s must not trigger a 60s local cooldown

data.description:
## Goal

Examine the llama-proxy restart rate: is ~24–34 full proxy restarts/day normal,
what causes each restart, which causes are avoidable, and which should be
fixed.

## Context / findings so far

- Studied 24h window (2026-10-14 14:02 → 2026-10-15 14:02 UTC): **30 full proxy
  restarts** ("Starting LLama Proxy Server"), of which **15 were mode-switch
  restarts** and the rest from other causes.
- Historical per-calendar-day restart counts (rotated logs identified by the
  same marker): 10-08=28, 10-09=22, 10-10=16, 10-11=10, 10-12=32, 10-13=24,
  10-14=34, 10-15=19 (partial, ~14h). So the rate is high but **consistent** —
  likely not unusual for this deployment, to be confirmed and explained.
- Non-mode-switch causes observed (to classify rigorously): llama-server death /
  self-heal ("llama-server process died, restarting..."), TTS watchdog events
  (note: TTS self-heal restarts only the TTS process, `backends/tts.py`
  `_attempt_tts_self_heal`; a full proxy start shortly after a TTS event needs
  explanation), operator-triggered restarts, log/rotation-driven signals.

## Questions to answer

1. What is the distribution of restart causes over ≥7 days (mode-switch,
   llama-server death/self-heal, TTS-watchdog-adjacent, manual/operator,
   crash)?
2. Is the restart rate unusual vs the historical baseline? (Preliminary: no.)
3. Which causes are avoidable (fixable) vs necessary?
4. Does restart churn correlate with local-qwen3 cooldown episodes and remote
   fallback spikes? (Preliminary: yes — 12/45 quarantine episodes followed a
   restart within 75s.)
5. What is the blast radius of a restart (restart duration, cold-prefill,
   in-flight work lost)?

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Restart causes are classified over ≥7 days with per-cause counts and at
      least one concrete log signature per class.
- [ ] A clear verdict on whether the studied period's restart rate is unusual.
- [ ] Avoidable vs necessary causes are separated, with a prioritised list of
      fixes (e.g. llama-server death root-cause, TTS exit-code=0 investigation,
      non-destructive mode switch).
- [ ] Any fixable cause has a follow-up work item created (or a decision not to
      act recorded).
- [ ] Evidence is reproducible (exact commands/log greps recorded in this
      item).

## References

- Related items: LP-0MRT928DD008136S (TTS watchdog loop),
  LP-0MS0Z9DTA003P6GB (TTS recovery state after llama restart),
  LP-0MS6OY4AA009O78D (restart reliability integration tests),
  LP-0MS6OYDKX004PT0U (fresh HTTP client after llama restart),
  LP-0MPY3DGGF0042178 (proxyctl restart), plus the sibling investigations for
  mode-flip frequency and cold-start grace period.
- Logs: `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*`.
data.title: Examine proxy restart frequency: is ~24-34 restarts/day normal and what causes them?
